title: The summary for Saturday 21 November
text:
Good morning, it is Saturday 21 November: this is the GERICO summary.

I begin with Iran. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi says Tehran still hopes diplomacy will end the war with the United States. Donald Trump responds that Iran wants a deal, but not one he can accept. Meanwhile, Washington has sanctioned four Iranian oil brokers. The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh.

In Ukraine, a double Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih killed a seven-year-old child and a female paramedic. Fifty-two people were injured, according to the regional governor. Trump says he had very good talks with Putin, but does not speak of security guarantees for Kyiv.

At the Antalya climate conference there is still no agreement. The latest draft no longer mentions fossil fuels, and a new text is expected today.

In brief. A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck central Peru, with no casualties reported. A Missouri judge has approved the $7.25 billion settlement with which Bayer settles the Roundup lawsuits. In Italy, the Court of Cassation has made definitive the life sentence for Gabriele Bianchi for the murder of Willy Monteiro Duarte.

Moving on to the markets. On Friday, Wall Street closed sharply lower, according to initial closing data. The Nasdaq lost 5.4%. The S&P 500 fell 3.8%, the Dow Jones 2%.

Weighing on the market was Nvidia, which shed around 13% following news of an SEC investigation into its accounting. Anthropic lost 8.5% on its second day of trading.

Earlier, European stock markets had closed sharply down. Milan lost 2.5%, Frankfurt 2.6%, Paris a little less than 2%, London 1%. In Tokyo, the close was around minus 5%. Agencies link the declines to fears over artificial intelligence.

On government bonds, the spread between BTPs and Bunds closed at 109.9 basis points, with the BTP yield at 4.4%.

On commodities, gold stood at $3,550, down more than 9% in a week and at a 14-month low. WTI crude oil closed in New York at $84. European gas exceeded €88 per megawatt-hour.

On foreign exchange, today's sources provide no verified data, so I am not reporting them.

Today is Saturday: stock markets are closed and there are no high-impact events on the agenda.

The complete news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
